caveats: Baseline-only diagnostic: candidate and raw oracle are absent; no independent equality claim.
Corrected eligibility changes initial missing coverage; legacy fixture timing is not an unchanged baseline.
Historical backfill still uses direct SQL with fixture provenance, bypassing historical agent grants/buffer/admission; live collection and ingestion are real.
Controlled historical cutoffs cross an hour, not actual wall-clock engine rollover.
Browser renderer shares the server VM; remote capable-client acceptance remains outstanding.
limitations: Sampled occupancy is not a query duration distribution.
No wait event includes runnable CPU and scheduler delay, not necessarily CPU execution.
Cumulative database counters can lag; Docker CPU windows can straddle phase boundaries.
Block I/O and CPU percentages do not prove I/O latency or throttling.
PostgreSQL track_io_timing is off; no per-query I/O duration is established.
Fresh fixture IDs, live dispatch phases, clock alignment and publication progress differ. Do not attribute every cross-run timing change solely to the overview correction.
There are 600 due intervals in this clock-aligned run versus 400 previously; every due interval is checked.
HTTP spans measure server work, while API/browser timings include client scheduling and transport; the browser and load generator share the two-vCPU server VM.
Trace cohorts use request starts, while ingestion acceptance histograms use completions.
The same repaired observer covers both measured phases and both latest controls.
